A real man apologizes for his mistakes when wrong was done but not intentional." I know it's semantics and sexist and etc, but what stuck was the intentions bit. It can sometimes be exhausting, sometimes there are a lot of things I can't do, and sometimes there are a lot of things I have to do because I make sure I try to do my best at everything, never half ass it. I do this not only because it is the right thing to do, but also because when something does go wrong and I do make a mistake I don't have to struggle to tear down the barrier of shame so I can admit I made a mistake and try and fix it. I stop, admit the mistake, make amends when appropriate, figure out what went wrong and why, try to fix the mistake and walk away with any lessons the mistake has taught me. Sometimes I'm not in the mindset, or too close to a situation to completely understand it and those lessons come as realizations later, but honesty, constant introspection and self forgiveness make my life much happier to live.
